name: python-repo-symbol-not-imported-asks
desc: `render` is a real symbol in app/render.py but the edited test file neither imports nor defines it — the 'real symbol, wrong scope' class the additive check structurally cannot see (it resolves repo-wide, so `render` is known and stays silent). enrolled_defs pins that `render` really is in the repo index, which is the firewall precondition: without it the check would abstain rather than fire
new:
import pytest


def test_digest():
    out = render(digest)
    assert out

name: python-module-function-called-without-qualifier-asks
desc: the module IS imported (`from app import utils`) but the call drops the qualifier: `utils.slugify(name)` becomes bare `slugify(name)`. File scope binds `utils`, not `slugify`. This is the second flavour of the class — the reference is wrong even though the file's import line looks right

name: python-symbol-imported-in-scope-clean
desc: same symbol, same call, but the edit imports it — correct usage stays silent. enrolled_defs pins render as reachable, so this silence is the in-scope rule dropping a live candidate rather than an enrollment that resolved nothing
new:
import pytest

from app.render import render


def test_digest():
    out = render(digest)
    assert out

name: python-hunk-scoped-out-of-scope-asks
desc: the CONTROL for the two abstain fixtures below: an Edit whose hunk is byte-identical to theirs, against a file carrying no abstain marker → ask. Replayed as an Edit, not a Write, so the added-lines set is the hunk ALONE. That is what makes the pairing meaningful: the abstain cases differ from this one only in the pre-edit file's text, so their silence is attributable to the whole-file read rather than to anything in the added text

name: python-star-import-abstains-clean
desc: `from app.render import *` binds an unknowable set, so the whole file abstains even though `render` is bare-called and is a repo symbol. The star import sits OUTSIDE the edited hunk, so only the pre-edit file read carries it — delete the wholeFile arm of the abstain and this fixture asks, matching its control above. This is the load-bearing false-positive gate: a miss is free, a false alarm is the adoption-killer

name: python-dynamic-binding-abstains-clean
desc: a `globals().update(...)` elsewhere in the file can introduce any name at runtime, so no static scan can enumerate the binding surface and the file abstains. Same whole-file-only placement as the star-import case, but through the pyDynamicBinding marker list rather than the star-import regex — and `globals` itself is a Python builtin, so the additive check has nothing to say about it either

name: python-dynamic-binding-control-asks
desc: the same file with the `globals().update(...)` line replaced by a plain qualified call, and the same hunk → ask. Pins that the silence above comes from the dynamic-binding marker specifically, not from anything else in that file (its `json` import, its two-def shape, or the edit's position)

name: go-file-scope-excluded-clean
desc: Go is out of scope in v1 — bare same-package calls resolve at compile time and would false-positive badly — so a Go file calling a repo symbol it does not import stays silent. The silence comes from the hook-side wrapper's language gate (cmd/runecho-guard/filescope.go), which short-circuits before the pure function is reached; the pure function gates again independently. Nothing else in the pipeline fires on this edit either
